skript.thema: Whirl: an open-source AI chat app you can host yourself

teile.name: Hook
teile.text: You can host your own multi-model AI assistant. Whirl publishes its full code under the MIT license. So what do you actually get, and what does it take?
teile.szene: Painted urban open-world poster style: a black-haired man in a black leather jacket and glowing cyan glasses opens a heavy toolbox in a neon-lit workshop, medium shot, warm lamp light, calm space above and below.

teile.name: Alle Modelle
teile.text: Start with the problem of juggling separate chat apps. Whirl routes every top model into one conversation through OpenRouter. You can adjust the thinking levels.
teile.szene: Painted urban game-poster style: a vintage telephone switchboard with many cables converging into one glowing socket, close shot, cyan and amber light, central focus, calm dark edges.

teile.name: Living Artifacts
teile.text: Say you're drafting a report. Documents, charts and full interactive pages open in a side panel. They stay editable, and you can share them by link.
teile.szene: Painted urban game-poster style: hands arranging paper sheets, a drafted chart and a small model on a drafting table beside an open side drawer, overhead medium shot, soft daylight, central action.

teile.name: Eigene Tools
teile.text: Need it to work with your own tools? Whirl connects to them over MCP. Installable skills teach it new tricks.
teile.szene: Painted urban game-poster style: the leather-jacketed presenter clicks a new tool onto a pegboard wall of wrenches and gadgets in a garage, medium shot, cyan glow reflecting on metal.

teile.name: Gedaechtnis
teile.text: Long-term memory carries your preferences and projects across chats. You don't start from scratch each time.
teile.szene: Painted urban game-poster style: a worn notebook with sticky notes and a small model city project lying on a desk at night, close shot, warm lamp light, calm space above and below.

teile.name: Gesperrte Chats
teile.text: Private topics? Locked chats are encrypted on your device with a password the server never sees. Only zero-retention models answer them.
teile.szene: Painted urban game-poster style: a brass padlock held shut in a gloved hand, a single key kept in a pocket, close shot, dramatic side light, rainy city blur behind.

teile.name: Die Huerde
teile.text: Here's the catch. To run it, you need Bun, a free Convex account, a Clerk application and an OpenRouter API key.
teile.szene: Painted urban game-poster style: four distinct keys and parts laid out in a row on a workbench while the presenter in cyan glasses studies them, medium shot, sparse tense lighting.

teile.name: Optionale Extras
teile.text: Extras like web search, billing and analytics switch on only with their own keys. Leave them out, and Whirl hides those features.
teile.szene: Painted urban game-poster style: a wall of old toggle switches where a few are flipped on and glowing while the rest stay dark, medium close shot, warm amber light, central focus.

teile.name: Fazit
teile.text: So can you host it yourself? The repository includes a self-hosting guide covering each step, locally and in production. We haven't tested it, so read the guide first. Be sure to like, share and save this video.
teile.szene: Painted urban game-poster style: the black-haired presenter in leather jacket and cyan glasses unrolls a large blueprint on a rooftop table at dusk, medium shot, warm restrained city glow.

regeln: Within each spoken phase use multiple distinct relevant shots, roughly 3-5 seconds each for Shorts; long videos can allow purposeful longer demonstrations. Preserve continuous narration and accurate subtitle timing.
A zoom, crop, subtitle change or decorative background does not count as a new motif. Never fill missing images with candles, unrelated stock or background-only frames.
Show the main image prominently; avoid tiny repeated photos in a mostly empty vertical frame. Preserve genuine evidence and important image details.
For AI Tools Explained identify the exact tool briefly, then show genuine interface views and different source-supported examples. Never present stock or an illustration as a real tool result.
Use original urban painted open-world-game poster styling for fictional scenes and presenters; no copied game characters. Match narrated action and era.

Clear speech and readable captions alone do not make a professional video. Inspect useful motif changes and narration-image alignment over the entire video. Missing main imagery is a substantial defect.
Include mandatory spoken like, share and save calls at the correct format-specific positions. Do not replace this requirement with a different CTA.

AI Tools Explained is for viewers with a practical task. Do not read parameter counts, architecture names, pipeline tags, context lengths or benchmark claims as a substitute for useful explanation. Explain the human task, the source-supported action and a concrete limit. A generic trending-tools question failed story review twice; prefer a specific visual workflow.

The user confirmed original presenter references on 2026-10-05: Business Origin Stories uses the blue-eyed man with a fedora, grey suit, dark tie and gold pocket watch; AI Tools Explained uses the black-haired man with black leather jacket and glowing cyan glasses. Preserve identity and typical clothing, vary action and setting.

Introduce the correct presenter at the opening and bring that same presenter back during the video in useful actions. Do not confine the figure to the ending. Do not replace original channel figures with different fictional people; anonymous period workers remain clearly illustrative supporting people, never a real-founder likeness.

Prefer vivid original painted open-world-game scenes to long holds on lifeless documentary photos. Preserve factual accuracy and show authentic tool examples briefly as evidence. Camera moves alone are not new motifs or full character animation.

The user confirmed on 2026-10-05 that both new delivered videos are much better than before. Preserve the original painted world, recurring channel identity, matching main imagery, music and useful scene changes. The long-term quality target remains 10/10; the user did not give these videos a numeric score. Do not replace their actual AI scores or the existing 7/10 delivery threshold with the aspirational target.

For AI Tools Explained Shorts comparable to the approved 82-second pilot, aim for 14-18 distinct relevant motifs instead of the previous 12 across 23 shots. Reduce repeated identical imagery and add genuinely different demonstrations, details or illustrative actions supported by the narration. Zooms, crops and label changes do not count as new motifs. This is a planning target, not a retroactive rejection of the positively received pilot.

For Business Origin Stories the user's latest refinement on 2026-10-05 is to aim for about 24 shots with 18 distinct relevant motifs for comparable 90-second Shorts. The delivered 24-shot/14-motif video was positively received; 18 motifs is the next improvement target, not its actual delivered count. Reduce repeats by adding four genuinely different relevant subjects or actions. Preserve useful pacing and the original channel character. Do not count zooms, crops or label changes as new motifs; adapt other video lengths to their story.
Explicit viewer feedback about our videos (not source facts): Es wurden einfach viel zu wenig Fotos verwendet
Pay off the specific opening question with a concrete, source-supported answer before the spoken like/share/save reminder. Generic praise is not a resolution.

Compare tools within a documented common role; never label a generative language model as a non-generative decision model just to fill a ranking. A title or hook must not promise hallucination-free results without explicit source support and scope.

Story revisions must preserve verified facts. Do not invent required GPUs, parameter counts, runtime guarantees or single-forward-pass behavior; resolve unsupported-detail warnings before treating a draft as ready. A critic's stronger hook or replacement tool is only a suggestion, never a source.
Vary sentence structure across ranked items and give each a distinct, source-supported use case without repetitive templates.
Omit dry metrics like star counts or download numbers unless they directly serve a crucial narrative purpose.
Build a clear narrative arc and relevant outros and calls-to-action instead of generic countdown filler; never invent stakes to improve a story score.
Use unique and specific hooks instead of overused generic tech creator tropes.
Avoid prolonged static shots of documentation or code scrolling; switch visuals dynamically to maintain pacing.
Use relevant, contextual visuals through the outro and CTA; verify that assets and screenshots match the technical reality of the software discussed.
Maintain consistency when citing engagement metrics by sticking to a single verified source type.
Keep all text elements safely within the inner title-safe zone and away from the top and bottom edges.
Ensure captions and subtitles have sufficient padding to avoid being clipped by screen interfaces.
skript.winkel: AI you can explore today - a concrete use case and an honest limitation for each tool

schwaechen: The sentence 'We haven't tested it, so read the guide first' hurts the authority of the review, making the recommendation feel incomplete or risky. Fix: Replace it with 'The repository provides a step-by-step guide to deploy it locally or in production.'

belege.text:
The AI chat app that sweats the details. Every top model, real memory, living documents, and your own tools. - 497 stars, license: MIT, created 2026-10-02
PRIMARY MODEL/PROJECT DESCRIPTION (not independently tested):
Whirl 

 
  The AI chat app that sweats the details. Every top model, real memory, 
  living documents, and your own tools, in one fast and friendly place.
 

 
   whirl.chat  ·
   Self-hosting  ·
   Architecture  ·
   Contributing 
 

---

Whirl is a full-stack AI chat app built on Next.js and Convex. It's the code
behind [whirl.chat](https://whirl.chat), published in full under the MIT
license. Read it, run your own, or help make it better.

## Features

- **Every top model** in one conversation, routed through
  [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai), with adjustable thinking levels.
- **Living artifacts:** documents, charts, and full interactive pages that
  stay editable in a side panel and can be shared by link.
- **Integrations** with your own tools over MCP (OAuth included), plus
  installable skills that teach Whirl new tricks.
- **Long-term memory** that carries preferences and projects across chats.
- **Live web search** and page reading for answers grounded in today's web.
- **Locked chats**, encrypted on your device with a password the server never
  sees, answered only by zero-retention models.
- **Incognito mode**, message queueing, voice input, image generation, file
  attachments, folders, sharing, and a lot of care around motion and polish.
- **Light and dark mode**, accent colors, and an installable mobile web app.

## Tech stack

Everything beyond Convex, Clerk, and OpenRouter is **optional** and switches
on with its own keys: billing (Autumn), web search (Exa), memory
(Supermemory), analytics (PostHog, Axiom), tracing (Braintrust), email
(Resend), and the support agent (Median). Leave them out and Whirl hides the
features they power. See [docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md).

## Quick start

You'll need [Bun](https://bun.sh), a free [Convex](https://convex.dev)
account, a [Clerk](https://clerk.com) application, and an
[OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai) API key.

Open [localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) and say hi. The
[self-hosting guide](docs/self-hosting.md) covers each step in detail,
including the Clerk JWT template Convex needs and how to deploy to
production.

## Repository layout

## Documentation

- [Self-hosting](docs/self-hosting.md): run Whirl locally and in production
- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md): every environment variable and
  what it switches on
- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): how a message travels from the
  composer to the model and back
- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): conventions, checks, and pull requests

## Contributing

Bug reports, ideas, and pull requests are all welcome. Start with
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), and please follow the
[code of conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Found a security issue? See
[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).
